title: Structured Cavity Quantum Electrodynamics
authors: Shunfa Liu, Jiantao Ma, Hanqing Liu, Yangpeng Wang, Xueshi Li, Haiqiao Ni, Zhichuan Niu, Kai Zou, Yun Meng, Xiaolong Hu, Xuehua Wang, Jin Liu
abstract: A cavity quantum electrodynamics (cQED) system consisting of a confined single photon and a single quantum emitter serves as a fundamental block for quantum optics and photonic quantum technologies. The canonical optical mode employed in the conventional cavity quantum electrodynamics features a uniform polarization distribution, leading to the scalar light-matter interaction in most existing experiments. Despite the rapid progress in the generation of structured light with spatially varied polarizations, the structured light-matter interaction, especially at the single quanta level, is highly intriguing yet largely unexplored. Here, we present the structured light-matter interaction at the single-photon level in a semiconductor cavity quantum electrodynamics system. Four distinct structured cavity modes that are spectrally close to each other are constructed in a micropillar cavity. By spatially locating a single epitaxial quantum dot (QD) at the periphery of a semiconductor micropillar cavity and spectrally tuning the QD emission wavelength into the resonances of the structured cavity modes, cavity-enhanced single-photon emissions with spin-locked chiral orbital angular momentum (OAM) and engineerable spin-orbit entanglements are achieved within a single wavelength-scale device. Our work opens an unexplored paradigm of structured quantum light-matter interactions and may further advance chiral quantum optics and high-dimensional photonic quantum technology.
summary: This paper reports on achieving controlled single-photon emission carrying spin-OAM entanglement within a semiconductor cavity QED system. By engineering structured optical modes in a micropillar, the researchers demonstrated that coupling a quantum dot dipole to specific resonances allows for dynamic generation and switching between different Bell states of entanglement. This opens a new paradigm for high-dimensional photonic quantum technologies.
main_problem: The research addresses the largely unexplored area of structured light-matter interaction at the single-photon level, moving beyond conventional scalar interactions in cavity QED.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated the generation and dynamic control of spin-orbit entangled single photons carrying chiral Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) using a chip-scale semiconductor cQED device.
method: The study combines theoretical modeling (FDTD simulations) with advanced experimental techniques, including polarization-resolved photoluminescence spectroscopy and quantum state tomography.
model_or_system: The physical platform is a semiconductor cavity QED system utilizing an epitaxial quantum dot coupled to structured modes ($	ext{M}1-	ext{M}4$) within a micropillar cavity. The mode structure arises from sidewall confinement, leading to vector vortex resonances.
key_observables: Spin-OAM entanglement (Bell states), Degree-of-circular-polarization ($D_{cp}$), OAM purity ($P_{	ext{OAM}}$), and Purcell enhancement factor ($\sim 4$).
important_parameters: Operating at cryogenic temperatures ($	ext{T} = 1.67 	ext{ K}$) under tunable magnetic fields (up to $\pm 9 	ext{ T}$); the coupling strength is tuned by matching QD emission to structured cavity resonances.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on modeling the mode structure using paraxial approximations corrected for sidewall confinement, which induces spin-orbit coupling effects.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematics of the cQED setup, PL spectra showing polarization selectivity and Purcell enhancement, near-field profiles confirming structured modes, and density matrices verifying tunable Bell states.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the necessity of studying structured light-matter interaction to detailing the physical realization in a micropillar cavity. It then systematically demonstrates mode selection using circular polarizations, followed by quantifying entanglement generation via state tomography across different resonance modes ($	ext{M}2$, $	ext{M}4$).
why_interesting: This work provides an excellent platform for AMO physicists studying open quantum systems, as it demonstrates coherent control over multiple degrees of freedom (spin and OAM) in a solid-state emitter coupled to engineered photonic environments.
